title: Merge Two Binary Trees
summary: Given two binary trees, root1 and root2, merge them into a new binary tree according to the following rules: if two nodes overlap, their values should be summed to form the new node value.
statement: Given two binary trees, root1 and root2, merge them into a new binary tree according to the following rules: if two nodes overlap, their values should be summed to form the new node value. If there is no overlap (i.e., one node is null), use the non-null node as part of the new tree. Begin the merging process from the root nodes of both trees.
constraints: Sum nodes at the same structural position; retain any position present in only one input.

hints: Tree positions, rather than array indices in the display, decide which values overlap.
For a pair of nodes, reuse the present subtree when only one exists; otherwise combine values and continue with both child pairs.
If either root is absent, return the other. Otherwise create a node with their sum and merge the left pair and right pair into its children.
A stack of input pairs and output nodes implements the recursive rule without a deep call stack.
editorial: Merge corresponding structural positions. A position occupied by both inputs gets the sum of the two values. A position occupied by one input retains that entire subtree. Do not simply add the displayed arrays by index: null placeholders and omitted trailing children make that incorrect. The iterative reference creates nodes for overlapping pairs and retains unmatched branches.
